title: Our homes aren't free until 2027. Where do we live after the wedding?
videoTitle: ASKING SEAN #278 | STAYING WITH FAMILY IS MORE SENSIBLE
excerpt: A couple marrying in 2026 each own a unit, but one is tenanted and the other is still being built. Sean weighs ending the tenancy, renting, buying a third home or moving in with family, and picks family.

qa.asker: YB, a viewer who wrote in by email
qa.context: YB marries in January 2026 and the couple want to move out of their parents' homes. His fiancée owns a completed condo in Cyberjaya, rented out at a small loss on a tenancy that runs through 2026; his own unit is under construction and due in 2027. He nets RM7,000 a month and together they earn about RM11,000. He has also found a new condo whose second phase he could just afford, at the cost of their lifestyle.
qa.question: Should they end the tenancy and move into her condo, rent a place, live with the in-laws for a year or two, or buy the new condo?
qa.quote: I think that living with the in-law first will be the best
qa.answer: Don't buy a third home for themselves now. Taking back her condo is acceptable, but Sean's choice is to live with her parents until his unit is ready in 2027, paying towards bills, and to keep the cash for the wedding, a baby and renovation.

reasons.title: The years around 30 burn cash
reasons.body: A wedding, a home and a first child come close together. A private delivery can cost RM10,000 to RM15,000, a confinement centre about RM15,000 to RM30,000, then childcare. Spare cash gives options; a stretched loan takes them away.

reasons.title: Move in with her parents, not yours
reasons.body: Sean found that tension usually runs between a mother and a daughter-in-law, so a husband moving in with his wife's family tends to be easier. Her mother can then help her with a newborn, which Sean found invaluable.

reasons.title: Family under one roof shares the load
reasons.body: Extra adults at home mean someone can watch the baby, and shared costs make help such as a cleaner affordable. Sean says the first three to six months with a newborn test everyone's energy.

reasons.title: Keep the tenanted unit earning
reasons.body: Ending a tenancy early means paying the tenant compensation under the agreement, typically about two months' rent. Sean also sees rents in Cyberjaya rising strongly, so the unit is worth keeping let.

actions: Hold off buying another own-stay home until your current one is ready.
Offer to pay utilities and treat the family to meals while you live with them.
Agree a move-out date with your spouse, such as when your own unit is handed over.
Set aside RM50,000 to RM80,000 to renovate an own-stay home for handover.
Price out childbirth, confinement and childcare before taking on any new commitment.
qa.caveat: If living with family would cause real friction, taking back the tenanted unit is Sean's acceptable second choice, provided it is convenient for work. His own experience of living with in-laws shapes this advice.
